Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

aRchtest 0.2.0

  • must_not_depend_on() now detects project functions that are passed as values: lapply(x, helper), purrr::map(x, helper), Reduce(helper, x), formals(helper) and Filter(helper, x) create a dependency edge to the module that defines helper, reported with resolved_by = "value". A name that a local binding shadows stays out of the graph, and a base or imported function passed by value is not tracked. A use written with backticks resolves the same way, so a non-syntactic name passed as a value such as load.sales is found (#21).
  • A rule without a selector is now rejected when it is checked, with the same “needs a selector first” wording the DSL uses when a constraint or an exclusion is added. Such a rule selects no file and can never produce a finding, so it failed with an internal error from the file matcher instead of a message that says what to fix (#27).
  • modules_excluding() subtracts files from a rule’s selection: the files a rule applies to are the union of its inclusion selectors minus the union of its exclusion selectors, so “only the API layer may call httr” can be written as modules_matching("R/*.R"), modules_excluding("R/api_*.R") and must_not_call(packages = "httr"). Exclusions combine, the check result and the rule’s formatted output list them, and an exclusion that removes every selected file fails with EMPTY SELECTION naming both pattern sets (#24).
  • File matching now uses PCRE (perl = TRUE) instead of TRE, so modules_matching_regex() accepts lookahead assertions such as ^R/(?!api_).*\\.R$ (#24).

aRchtest 0.1.0

Initial release. aRchtest declares architectural boundaries between the modules of an R project as data and enforces them as ordinary testthat tests.

New features

  • arch_check() takes a single rule or a list of them and returns an arch_result carrying a data.table of violations with one row per finding: rule, file, line, column, enclosing function, callee, resolved owner, how it was resolved, an internal-API flag and the source text of the call. A clean check returns an empty table with the same columns and types, never NULL. The project is discovered, parsed and resolved once per check regardless of how many rules are supplied.
  • arch_expect() wraps the same check as a testthat expectation.
  • arch_violations() accesses the violations table.
  • print() and format() methods give a readable summary grouped by rule.
  • modules_matching() and modules_matching_regex() narrow a rule to a set of files, by glob or by regular expression, relative to the project root.
  • must_not_call() forbids packages, individual functions, or both.
  • must_not_depend_on() forbids a dependency on other modules of the same project, so domain/ can be held away from infra/.
  • rule() starts a rule with a name and an optional rationale. A rule is inert data: building one performs no analysis.
  • Rules compose with the base R pipe; no magrittr or tidyverse dependency.

Resolution

  • The engine reads parse data only and never sources, loads or evaluates the code under analysis, so checks are deterministic and work on a project that does not currently run.
  • Declared dependencies come from DESCRIPTION for a package project and from library()/require() calls for a Shiny app, plumber API or script project.
  • Unqualified calls are resolved against declared dependencies, so a rule cannot be evaded by dropping the :: prefix. Local definitions win over package exports.
  • Base packages count as declared, so must_not_call(functions = "system") fires on a bare system() call.
  • A symbol exported by more than one candidate is reported as ambiguous rather than guessed at, and on_ambiguous = "fail" makes ambiguity a violation.
  • Calls that cannot be attributed are counted, never reported as violations, and the resolution counts are part of every result.
  • A dependency whose exports cannot be enumerated degrades resolution visibly rather than erroring or reporting a falsely clean project.
  • A file that does not parse is reported with a warning and skipped; the check still covers every other file and says the analysis was partial.
  • A selector that matches no file fails the check rather than passing silently.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • arch_check() and arch_expect() find the project root when root is not given: they walk up from the working directory to the nearest directory holding a DESCRIPTION or an .Rproj file, and under R CMD check use the package sources in <pkg>.Rcheck/00_pkg_src/<pkg>. Previously the default root = "." pointed at tests/testthat under testthat, so the README example failed with EMPTY SELECTION on clean code. An explicit root is still used as given (#19).
  • The EMPTY SELECTION message names the root the rule was checked against, so a wrong root is no longer reported as a wrong pattern (#19).
